measurement: How far are unattributable POI from their nearest city?
question_being_tested: 1,314,927 materialised POI carry no city attribution. Is the population-scaled radius (20/12/7/4km by city size) the binding constraint, in which case widening it recovers legitimate pages, or are those POI genuinely rural, in which case widening would invent attributions?
method: For every POI in DE, FR, PL and GB that carries no area polygon AND falls outside every city radius, compute the great-circle distance to the nearest city in the 31,715-city gazetteer and record that city's population.
conclusion: LEAVE THE RADIUS AS IT IS. Three independent readings of the same data agree.
reasoning: 65 per cent of these POI sit 12km or more from the nearest city, and 38 per cent sit beyond 20km. No defensible radius reaches them. A page claiming a POI 20km outside a town is in that town is false, and falseness is the thing the gates exist to stop.

The classes that dominate the residue are rural by nature: 66,280 mountain peaks, 30,169 memorials, 12,654 archaeological sites. These are not misattributed urban POI; they are features of open country. OSM maps the countryside as densely as it maps cities, and the countryside has no city to belong to.

For 64 per cent of them the nearest city is under 35,000 people, which carries a 4km radius. The only bucket a widening could touch is 0-5km, which is 26,026 POI, 4.9 per cent of the residue. Spread across several thousand small towns that is single-digit POI per town, far below every density threshold any aggregation shape requires, so even an attribution that were true would produce almost no accepted page.
what_would_be_wrong_about_widening: A restaurant 4.5km outside a 10,000-person town is not a restaurant in that town. Attributing it to the town to raise the candidate count is the geographic form of the city-name swapping the brief prohibits: the page name would change while the underlying fact did not.
legitimate_alternative_recorded_not_buil: These POI are reachable by a page type keyed on the thing they actually belong to rather than on a city: a national park, a mountain range, a long-distance trail, a coastline, an administrative district. That is a different family with its own source and demand requirements, not a loosening of city attribution. It is recorded in the gap analysis as a data/family path, unmeasured and unbuilt.
